To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
research and teaching of the past and problem history of psychology are declining in the German-speaking area, but that this decline is probably not irreversible.

(a) the research community of psychologists in the German-speaking area has published fewer articles on the history of their subject since the 1993 than before; (b) the research community in the United States has published less on the history of its subject since the 1980s than before; and (c) the teaching of the subject in both countries has been less frequent in the last decades than before.

(1) research on and teaching the history of psychology have been and still are important for the development of psychology, (2) there are still many opportunities to improve the situation, and (3) the future is bright.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether psychology is becoming an unhistorical discipline and, in the sense of the title, whether it is becoming an “unhistorical” science.
the question: What is the future of the history of the history of science?
the question: Is psychology becoming a more unhistorical science?

the history of psychology has not become an unhistorical science, as the title suggests.
psychology as a science is becoming an unhistorical discipline, and this trend should be stopped.
psychology is becoming an unhistorical discipline.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the history of psychology has to become a “big data history of psychology” (BDHP) in the sense of a “big history of psychology” in order to be able to cope successfully with the challenges of a globalized world.
psychology is becoming an unhistorical, i.e., a non-reflective science, which, however, is a very dangerous and problematic development.

the history of psychology has to be taught in psychology courses and research on the history of the discipline has to be supported in order to keep the discipline alive and to prevent it from becoming an unhistorical discipline.
